newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Esso Australia 1996 net profit A$635 mln.
newsitem.headline: Esso Australia 1996 net profit A$635 mln.

text.p: Esso Australia Resources Ltd, a wholly-owned unit of Exxon Corp, on Thursday reported a net profit after abnormal items of A$635 million for calendar 1996, up from A$430 million in 1995.
The bottom line result included a A$159 million after-tax abnormal gain from the settlement of a resource-tax dispute.
Revenue grew 19 percent to A$2.2 billion, reflecting a rise in average crude oil prices of about US$3.30 to US$21.50 a barrel in 1996, Esso said.
Esso's net liquids production from the Bass Strait oilfields off the coast of Victoria and central Australia averaged 129,000 barrels per day in 1996, down 11 percent from 1995, it said.
Gas sales from Bass Strait and central Australia also fell.
They averaged 322 million cubic feet per day in 1996, 10 percent lower than in 1995, it added.
Esso managing director Charles Fields said in a statement the lower gas sales were due to reduced demand from Victoria state's electricity-generating sector.
Production from West Tuna and Bream B platforms, installed in Bass Strait last year, will give Esso an extra 25,000 barrels per day of oil output when they reach full output, he said.
Esso owns the Bass Strait fields50/50 with The Broken Hill Co Pty Ltd. Esso operates the fields.
